description: Trimble GNSS Planning Online is a free web application from Trimble for planning satellite surveys and field work by predicting which navigation satellites will be visible from a place at a given time. Users set the location, date and time span and an elevation cut-off angle in the settings, and the tool, driven by the current almanac, presents a satellite list, charts over time, a sky plot of satellite tracks and world maps, and a separate view of ionospheric effects; the interface is available in several languages. Surveyors, engineers and drone or machine-control operators use such planning to choose times with enough satellites and good geometry, measured as dilution of precision, especially near buildings, terrain or other obstructions. Coverage: worldwide. Format and access: browser application, free, no sign-in seen. Caveats: predictions assume open sky or a simple cut-off and do not model detailed obstructions or interference; the list of constellations covered was not visible in the page text read, and outputs cannot be exported as data. Simulation uses: estimating satellite visibility and geometry when planning positioning-dependent operations, such as surveys after a disaster or timing-critical work, and reference values for hazard exposure to poor geometry or ionospheric disturbance. Related records: the Galileo quarterly performance reports give measured service performance, and OPUS and CSRS-PPP process the data collected.
